title: The dance of the bees
text: When a honeybee finds a field of flowers, it returns to the hive and {{1}} a dance on the vertical comb. Other bees crowd round, touching the dancer with their antennae, and from the performance they {{2}} both the direction and the distance of the food. The angle of the dance, measured against the vertical, {{3}} the angle between the sun and the flowers; the length of the waggling run indicates how far to fly. Karl von Frisch, who {{4}} this code in the 1940s, initially met disbelief: the idea that an insect could {{5}} abstract information in symbols seemed to put language where it did not belong. The sceptics lost. Decades of experiments — robots rigged to dance false directions, bees faithfully flying to the {{6}} locations — confirmed the grammar of the dance almost completely. The system has limits that human languages do not {{7}}: a bee cannot discuss last week's flowers or imagine next year's, and it cannot lie — or can it? Researchers have watched foragers dance enthusiastically about patches that {{8}} to be empty, though whether from error or from genuine dishonesty nobody is quite sure.

gaps.explanation: 'performs a dance' — the standard collocation; you carry out a task, fulfil a promise and achieve a goal, but you perform a dance.
'they extract both direction and distance' — take the information out of the performance; extricate = free from a tangle, retract = withdraw.
'the angle matches the angle between the sun and the flowers' — corresponds exactly; agree and coincide would need 'with', and rivals expresses competition, not equivalence.
'who decoded this code' — worked out what the signals meant; declare and decline are formal near-forms that do not fit 'code'.
'could encode abstract information in symbols' — convert it into a code; enclose = surround or attach.
'bees faithfully flying to the indicated locations' — the ones the dance had pointed to.
'limits that human languages do not share' — do not have as well; shape = mould, and shave and shake are irrelevant to the meaning.
'patches that turned out to be empty' — proved to be; 'turn out' is the fixed verb, and the prefixed forms do not combine with 'out to be'.
